newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P affirms Venantius AA+ foreign currency rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms Venantius AA+ foreign currency rating.

text.p: U.S. credit rating agency Standard & Poor's (S&P) said on Thursday it affirmed the AA+ foreign currency rating of Swedish state-owned credit market company Venantius AB.
The agency said Venantius's foreign currency outlook was stable derived from the stable oulook for its parent, the Kingdom of Sweden, and its expected fiscal strengthening.
It also affirmed Venantius' AAA local currency rating and A-1+ short term ratings.

"The affirmation follows the government's announcement that Venantius will take over the shares in Securum AB and the responsibility for winding up remaining assets in the Securum group," S&P said in a statement.
Securum assumed responsibility for large non-performing assets from state-controlled Nordbanken and Gota Bank during the financial crisis in the early 1990s.
Assets in the Securum group are expected to be a stake in chemical group Akzo Nobel NV, property holdings, a loan portfolio and cash, S&P said.
The loan portfolio may take some time to wind up but other assets are expected to be sold relatively quickly, it said.
"Venantius will maintain the strong backing of the Kingdom (of Sweden) by way of its equity investment, funding facilities and net worth guarantee," S&P said.
The higher sovereign local currency rating and stable outlook reflect the government's flexibility in taxing, its influence over monetary matters and its commitment to low inflation, the agency said.
